full_judgment:
3. The petitioner, on receiving the letter of the DCT, has filed the writ petition stating that the demand was made under section 55(1) of the VAT Act without issuing any previous show cause notice; that the demand is illegal and not sustainable in law; that as per section 55 of the VAT Act, the demand has to be made within three years from the date of occurrence, but the impugned demand has been made beyond the period of three years and, as such, it is barred by limitation. 

 5. Mr. ARM Quiyum Khan, the learned Advocate for the petitioner appearing with Mr. Md. Ali Akbor Khan, takes us through the writ petition, the connected materials on record and submits that from the impugned demand letter, it is evident that the demand was made under section 55(1) of the VAT Act, but no previous notice was issued to the petitioner demanding VAT. He next submits that the demand from 6-7-1994 to 6-7-2000 is barred by limitation. He also submits that the petitioner would pay the amount of less paid/unpaid VAT for the period from 7-7-1999 to 6-7-2000 which is not barred by limitation, if it is informed to the petitioner by the VAT authority. 

 7. In reply, Ms Israt Jahan, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing with Ms. Nurun Nahar and Mr. Swamp Kanti Dev, the learned Assistant Attorney-Generals, frankly concedes that part of the demand was not made within three years from the date of occurrence as required under the then provision of section 55 of the VAT Act. She adds that in the notice, the word ফাকি has also been used and therefore, it is a case of evasion of VAT and, as such, there is no limitation for demanding the evaded VAT amount under section 37 of the VAT Act. However, ongoing through the demand letter dated 7-7-2002 (Annexure-E to the writ petition), Ms. Israt Jahan admits that the demand was made under section '55(1) of the VAT Act, but it ought to have been made under section 37 of the VAT Act. Ms Israt Jahan further adds that order may be passed for payment of VAT for the periods from 7-7-1999 to 6-7-2000 which is not barred by limitation and the Rule may be disposed of accordingly. 

 13. The demand was made on 7-7-2002. Thus, it is evident that the demand for the periods between September, 1994 up to 6th July, 1999 is barred by limitation and the demand for the periods between 7th July, 1999 to June, 2000 is well within time. Therefore, the petitioner is liable to pay VAT for the said period. 

 15. For the reasons discussed hereinbefore, we are of the view that the Rule may be disposed of with a direction to the customs authority to calculate and inform the petitioner the amount of VAT payable by it for the periods, which is not barred by limitation.
